rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Fluid-mosaic: phospholipid bilayer + integral/peripheral protein + cholesterol + glycocalyx
Protein secretion: ribosome → RER → Golgi → vesicle → exocytosis
Mitochondrial respiration: glycolysis → Krebs → ETS → ~34 ATP

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Cell wall vs cell membrane:** the wall is outside, rigid, fully permeable, non-living; the membrane is living, selective, and the true gatekeeper of the cell.  ·  **Cristae vs thylakoids:** cristae are folds of the mitochondrial *inner membrane*; thylakoids are separate flattened discs *inside* the chloroplast stroma, stacked into grana.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The organelle-discovery table (Hooke → Brown → Golgi → Benda → Porter → Palade → de Duve → Singer & Nicolson) is a reliable 2–3 mark source in very-short-answer sections.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Pancreatic acinar cell** — RER-rich; exports digestive enzymes.  ·  **Liver cell (hepatocyte)** — SER-rich; detoxifies drugs and alcohol.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Endomembrane system flow:** nucleus → RER → Golgi (cis→trans) → vesicles → membrane/lysosome/secretion — the cell's production line.  ·  **Compartmentalisation again:** lysosome pH ~5 vs cytosol pH ~7.2 is why suicide bags stay harmless until they rupture.  ·  **Semi-autonomous organelles:** mitochondria and chloroplasts carry circular DNA + 70S ribosomes and divide by fission — the endosymbiotic signature.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Cell wall: cellulose (plants), chitin (fungi), peptidoglycan (bacteria); middle lamella → primary → secondary; fully permeable.  ·  Membrane: fluid-mosaic model (Singer & Nicolson 1972) — phospholipid bilayer + integral/peripheral proteins + cholesterol + glycocalyx; selective permeability, transport, signalling.  ·  Mitochondria: double membrane, cristae with oxysomes, matrix with Krebs enzymes + circular DNA + 70S ribosomes; aerobic respiration → ATP ("powerhouse").  ·  Plastids: chloroplast (photosynthesis), chromoplast (colour), leucoplast (storage: amylo/elai/aleuroplast); grana = thylakoid stacks in stroma.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Membrane thickness ≈ 7–8 nm; mitochondrion ≈ 0.5–1 µm; ribosome ≈ 15–20 nm.  ·  About 50 acid hydrolases are packed in lysosomes.

rows.text: **Muscle cell** — sarcoplasmic reticulum stores Ca²⁺ for contraction; mitochondria dense between myofibrils.  ·  **Potato tuber amyloplast** — leucoplast storing starch.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: 9+2 axoneme (cilia/flagella); 9+0 centriole  ·  RER: ribosome-studded cisternae — protein synthesis for export; SER: tubules — lipids, steroids, detox, Ca²⁺ (sarcoplasmic reticulum).  ·  Golgi (Golgi 1898): cis face receives from ER, modifies (glycosylation), trans face ships — vesicles, lysosomes, cell plate.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Lysosomes (de Duve): acid hydrolases at pH ~5; digestion, autophagy, autolysis — "suicide bags".  ·  Ribosomes (Palade 1953): rRNA + protein, no membrane; 80S = 60S+40S (eukaryote), 70S = 50S+30S (prokaryote/organelles); polysomes; translation.  ·  Nucleus (Brown 1831): double envelope + pores, nucleolus (rRNA factory), chromatin (eu- vs heterochromatin) → chromosomes with centromere; metacentric/submetacentric/acrocentric/telocentric.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Cilia/flagella: 9+2 microtubule axoneme from basal bodies; cilia short/numerous/oar-like, flagella long/few/undulating.  ·  Inclusions: starch, glycogen, fat droplets, protein crystals, pigments, crystals — non-living stores; plant central vacuole maintains turgor.  ·  **Lysosome vs vacuole:** lysosomes are single-membraned enzyme sacs for digestion; the plant central vacuole is mainly storage/turgor, though it also contains hydrolases.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **RER vs SER:** ribosomes on the surface define RER and protein synthesis; smooth tubules without ribosomes make lipids and detoxify.  ·  **Cilia vs flagella:** same 9+2 axoneme, but cilia are short, numerous and beat like oars; flagella are long, few and undulate.  ·  **Nucleolus vs nucleus:** the nucleolus is a membraneless sub-region of the nucleus that makes rRNA/ribosomes — not a separate organelle.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Inclusions vs organelles:** inclusions (starch, fat, crystals) are non-living, non-membrane-bound deposits; organelles are living, organised functional structures.  ·  **Tomato chromoplast** — carotenoid pigments colour the ripe fruit.  ·  **Tracheal ciliated epithelium** — cilia sweep mucus; destroyed by smoking.
